From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Performance SLO & Context Window follow-up \u0014 FinCo demo

Thanks again for the call today \u0014 great to meet the team. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can align on performance targets and PoC scope.

Call summary:
- Use case: customer support assistant that ingests past conversations (avg 2\u20134k tokens historical context) + current prompt.
- Expected output length: typically 100\u2013400 tokens; occasional long responses up to ~1,000 tokens for policy explanations.
- Key SLOs discussed: p95 latency target for end-to-end user-facing responses, streaming enabled to reduce TTF-first-byte.
- Expected concurrency/throughput: steady-state 30 reqs/sec with bursts to 150 concurrent sessions during peak events.

FinCo asks we captured:
1) p95 latency <= 250ms for 2\u20133k token input + 200\u2013400 token output (streaming preferred).
2) Support for context windows up to 8k tokens with predictable latency impact.
3) Ability to scale concurrency to ~150 active sessions and graceful degradation (fallback to smaller model variant) under capacity.

What Redwood recommends / next steps:
- Benchmark test: we\u2019ll run a short performance benchmark against representative payloads you share (we've done similar tests in our dedicated infra). Please provide 3 sample prompts: 1 short, 1 mid (~300 tokens), 1 long (~2.5k tokens).
- Streaming: enable chunked token streaming (we provide SSE/WebSocket) to improve perceived latency; this typically gives first-byte in <50ms for short outputs even if full generation takes longer.
- Context-window tradeoffs: larger context windows (>=4k tokens) increase KV cache memory and attention compute; expect p95 to increase nonlinearly with input length \u0014 we\u2019ll quantify on the benchmark.
- Safety: we'll redact any PII you don't want in logs; audit logs and isolated Dedicated pools available for Private deployment discussion.

Attachments: redwood-performance-matrix.pdf (performance by model/context), finco-mutual-action-plan.xlsx (MAL with deliverables/timelines).

Proposed timeline:
- You share sample payloads + rough traffic profile by Tue 30 Jun.
- We run benchmarks and return results + config recommendations by Fri 3 Jul.
- Optional: 2-week POC targeting peak concurrency and streaming behavior.

Can you confirm the sample payloads and whether procurement needs to be looped in now for a PoC?

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0142

Thanks Marissa \u0014 helpful recap. A couple clarifications from our side before we share payloads:

1) Latency target: p95 <= 250ms is our ideal for interactive chat, but we can accept a higher p95 for very long-context queries (e.g., >6k tokens). Can you give ballpark expected p95s across 1k / 3k / 6k input sizes for the models you suggested?

2) Streaming: we absolutely need first-byte streaming under 100ms for UX on our web client. Full completion can be slower, but first-byte matters.

3) Concurrency: 150 concurrent sessions is peak. Average concurrency probably 30\u201340. We need to understand cost tradeoffs if you recommend sharding across model variants for cost/latency.

4) Security: procurement asked if you can provide SOC 2 Type II + confirmation that request/response logs can be disabled or routed to customer-managed storage.

We'll aim to get sample payloads to you by Mon 29 Jun. Looping in procurement (procurement@finco.com) for contract/pre-POC questions.

Thanks,
Aaron

Aaron \u0014 thanks, and great questions. Looping Dylan (infra/perf) to add concrete numbers and propose bench configs. High-level answers while Dylan runs the tests: 

- Ballpark p95 (end-to-end, hosted Redwood API, using our recommended 13B quantized family):
  * ~1k input + 150 token output: p95 ~ 90\u2013120ms (first-byte <40ms with streaming enabled)
  * ~3k input + 300 token output: p95 ~ 180\u2013260ms (first-byte ~50\u201380ms streaming)
  * ~6k input + 500 token output: p95 ~ 350\u2013600ms (first-byte can still be <100ms depending on caching)

Notes on context-window impact:
- KV cache: longer inputs increase memory and per-token attention compute; for long contexts we see superlinear latency growth if the model must attend across the full window each generation step.
- Sampling & output length: output token count affects total time; streaming enables UX-first-byte improvements while generation continues.
- Quantization: int8/int4 profiles reduce latency and memory but can change accuracy; we\u2019ll include quality regression checks in the bench.

Dylan \u2014 can you run two quick benchmarks on our Dedicated infra:
- Config A: 13B quantized, context 1k/3k/6k, output caps 150/300/500, concurrency 1/10/50 (single-worker profile).
- Config B: 7B optimized (lower-latency variant) same inputs as above to compare tradeoffs (cost vs latency).

Aaron/Priya \u2014 if you can drop the sample prompts and a short traffic profile in the Drive folder above, we\u2019ll run these and push results + recommended config by Fri. Also confirming: SOC 2 Type II is available and request/response logging can be disabled or sent to customer-managed S3 (we\u2019ll put that option in the MAL).

Next steps we propose:
1) FinCo: upload sample payloads + traffic profile to the Drive folder (by EOD Mon 29 Jun).
2) Redwood: run bench and return p95/p50/p99, first-byte times, resource profile, and config recs (by Fri).
3) Optional: 2-week PoC (Dedicated) to validate at peak concurrency and streaming UX.

Thanks \u2014 Marissa
